WATER SECURITY IN THE BENGAL DELTA: POLLUTION CHALLENGES AND DECENTRALIZED WATER MANAGEMENT

Journal: Water Conservation and Management (WCM)
Author: Akram Hossain, Mohammad Razib Mustafiz, Tanjina Noushin, Touhid Bhuiyan
Print ISSN : 2523-5664

ABSTRACT

Water resource security across the multi-channel deltaic landscape of Bangladesh is severely threatened by overlapping geogenic, industrial, municipal, and hydro-climatic pollution vectors. Deep aquifer extraction continues to expose rural populations to geogenic arsenic (As) mobilization, while urban river systems—particularly the Buriganga and Shitalakkhya—suffer from unchecked industrial point-source discharges. These effluents introduce hazardous concentrations of lead (Pb), cadmium (Cd), and hexavalent chromium (Cr⁶⁺) that exceed safety limits and bioaccumulate across aquatic trophic levels. In southwestern coastal zones, sea-level rise and diminished upstream freshwater inputs drive shallow aquifer salinity fronts inland, compounding public health risks through elevated rates of gestational hypertension. On a macro-scale, monsoonal precipitation variations interact with deficient urban drainage to cause persistent water-logging, which mixes unmanaged municipal solid waste and fecal sludge into shallow domestic wells. Concurrently, agricultural runoff laden with reactive nitrogen and phosphorus drives widespread eutrophication across eco-sensitive wetland (haor) basins, depleting dissolved oxygen and lowering fish biodiversity. To bridge the gap between regional diagnostics and scalable technical solutions, this paper evaluates the engineering formulations of localized treatment practices. We model the orthokinetic kinetics of household alum coagulation, analyze cross-flow reverse osmosis under the solution-diffusion model to identify calcium sulfate (CaSO₄) scaling thresholds, and define the thermodynamic constraints of solar-driven distillation. Finally, we highlight critical regulatory and telemetry gaps, proposing a strategic shift toward automated, IoT-enabled decentralized water networks that integrate solar-assisted electrocoagulation cells with passive phytoremediation wetlands to secure long-term deltaic water safety.
